title: From the return to the Jewish revolts, and the Americas of the Book of Mormon, 539 BCE–400 CE
reviewed: 2026-10-18. Each quote was copied from the linked article and is checked by npm run verify:sources.

events.title: Darius the Great rules Persia
events.summary: Darius reorganizes the Persian Empire into provinces. Ezra 6 says he let the temple in Jerusalem be finished.

source.quote: reigning from 522 BCE until his death in 486 BCE

events.title: The Behistun Inscription
events.summary: Darius carves his story on a cliff in three languages. It later became the key to reading cuneiform.

source.quote: sometime between his coronation as king of the Persian Empire in the summer of 522 BC and his death in autumn of 486 BC

events.title: Xerxes I, the Ahasuerus of Esther
events.summary: Xerxes rules Persia from Susa and Persepolis. Many identify him with King Ahasuerus in the book of Esther.

source.quote: reigning from 486 BC until his assassination in 465 BC

events.title: Greece defeats Xerxes at Salamis
events.summary: The Athenian fleet wrecks the Persian navy in a narrow strait. Xerxes retreats to Asia.

source.quote: a naval battle fought in 480 BC

events.title: Artaxerxes I sends Ezra and Nehemiah
events.summary: The Persian king of Ezra 7 and Nehemiah 2 rules for forty years. He faces a long revolt in Egypt.

source.quote: from August 465 to December 424 BC

events.title: Herodotus writes his Histories
events.summary: A Greek traveler writes the first great history of the Persian Wars. He describes Babylon, Egypt, and Persia.

source.quote: 425 BC) was a Greek historian and geographer

events.title: The Jewish garrison at Elephantine
events.summary: Jewish soldiers guard Egypt's southern border for Persia. Their letters name Sanballat and the high priest Johanan.

source.quote: stationed at Elephantine under Achaemenid rule, 495-399 BCE

events.title: Athens tries and executes Socrates
events.summary: The philosopher is condemned for impiety and corrupting the youth. He drinks hemlock.

source.quote: The Trial of Socrates (399 BC)

events.title: Alexander besieges Tyre
events.summary: Alexander builds a causeway to the island city and takes it after seven months. Ezekiel 26 foretold Tyre's ruin.

source.quote: The siege of Tyre was carried out by Alexander the Great in 332 BC

events.title: Alexander founds Alexandria
events.summary: A new Greek city rises on Egypt's coast. It becomes home to the largest Jewish community outside Judea.

source.quote: Founded in 331 BC by Alexander the Great

events.title: The Ptolemies rule Egypt and Judea
events.summary: Alexander's general Ptolemy founds a Greek dynasty in Egypt. Judea lies under its rule for a century.

source.quote: It was founded in 305 BC by the Macedonian Greek general Ptolemy I Soter

events.title: The Torah is translated into Greek
events.summary: Jews in Alexandria translate the books of Moses into Greek. The Septuagint becomes the Bible of the early Church.

source.quote: at the request of Ptolemy II Philadelphus (285-247 BC)

events.title: Antiochus IV outlaws the Jewish faith
events.summary: The Seleucid king bans the Sabbath and circumcision. He sets up a pagan altar in the temple.

source.quote: Seleucid King Antiochus IV Epiphanes launched a campaign of repression against the Jewish religion in 168 BCE.

events.title: The Maccabees retake the temple
events.summary: Judas Maccabeus leads a revolt against Seleucid rule. The temple is cleansed in 164 BCE, the origin of Hanukkah.

quote: The main phase of the revolt lasted from 167 to 160 BCE
In 164 BCE, the Maccabees captured Jerusalem

events.title: The Hasmonean kingdom of Judea
events.summary: The Maccabees' family rules Judea as priests and kings. Herod ends the line with Roman help.

quote: Simon Thassi established the dynasty in 141 BC
Herod the Great displaced the last reigning Hasmonean client-ruler in 37 BC.

events.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls are copied
events.summary: Scribes copy and hide hundreds of scrolls near the Dead Sea. They hold the oldest known copies of most Old Testament books.

source.quote: Dating from the 3rd century BCE to the 1st century CE

events.title: Pompey takes Jerusalem for Rome
events.summary: A Roman general settles a Hasmonean civil war by force. Judea becomes a Roman client state.

source.quote: The siege of Jerusalem in 63 BC occurred during the campaigns of Roman general Pompey the Great

events.title: Herod the Great becomes king of Judea
events.summary: Rome's client king takes Jerusalem and rules with an iron hand. Matthew 2 sets the birth of Jesus in his last years.

source.quote: consulship of Agrippa and Gallus (37 BCE)

events.title: Herod builds Caesarea and its harbor
events.summary: Herod builds a great artificial harbor on an open coast. Caesarea becomes Rome's seat in Judea and Paul's prison.

source.quote: In 22 BCE, Herod began construction of a deep-sea harbour named Sebastos

events.title: Herod rebuilds the temple
events.summary: Herod enlarges the temple and its courts on a vast new platform. This is the temple Jesus taught in.

source.quote: Herod's work on the Temple is generally dated from 20/19 BCE until 12/11 or 10 BCE.

events.image: File:Monnaie - Bronze, Incertain, Judée, Hérode Archelaos - btv1b8498504d (1 of 2).jpg
events.title: Herod Archelaus rules Judea
events.summary: Herod's son rules Judea until Rome deposes him. Matthew 2 says Joseph feared him and settled in Nazareth.

source.quote: 4 BC to AD 6)

events.title: The census of Quirinius
events.summary: Rome counts Judea's people and property for taxes. Luke 2 links a census under Quirinius to Jesus's birth.

source.quote: a census of the Roman province of Judaea taken in 6 CE

events.title: Tiberius becomes emperor
events.summary: Augustus's stepson rules the empire. Luke 3 dates John the Baptist's preaching to his fifteenth year.

source.quote: was the second Roman emperor from AD 14 until his death

events.title: Caiaphas becomes high priest
events.summary: Rome's prefect appoints Caiaphas high priest. He presides when Jesus is brought before the council.

source.quote: According to Josephus, Caiaphas was appointed in AD 18 by the Roman prefect Valerius Gratus

events.image: File:Monnaie - Bronze, Incertain, Judée, Hérode Antipas - btv1b84985015 (1 of 2).jpg
events.title: Herod Antipas rules Galilee
events.summary: Herod's son rules Galilee during Jesus's ministry. He beheads John the Baptist. Caligula exiles him in 39.

source.quote: In 39 Antipas was accused by his nephew Agrippa I of conspiracy against Emperor Caligula

events.title: Pontius Pilate governs Judea
events.summary: The Roman prefect governs from Caesarea for ten years. A stone found there in 1961 bears his name.

source.quote: these are traditionally dated from 26 to 36/37

events.title: Philo of Alexandria pleads before Caligula
events.summary: The Jewish philosopher leads an embassy after riots in Alexandria. His writings shaped early Christian thought.

source.quote: a delegation to the Roman emperor Caligula in 40 CE

events.title: Herod Agrippa I rules Judea
events.summary: Claudius gives Herod's grandson all of Judea. Acts 12 says he killed James and died suddenly at Caesarea.

source.quote: Agrippa I died suddenly from an "infestation of worms" in 44.

events.title: The Delphi inscription names Gallio
events.summary: A letter of Claudius names Gallio as governor of Achaia. It helps date Paul's stay in Corinth in Acts 18.

source.quote: a letter written by the Roman emperor Claudius in 52 CE

events.title: Felix governs Judea
events.summary: The Roman procurator holds Paul at Caesarea for two years, as Acts 24 tells.

source.quote: was the fourth Roman procurator of Judea Province in 52-60

events.title: Festus sends Paul to Caesar
events.summary: The new procurator hears Paul with King Agrippa II. Paul appeals to Caesar and sails for Rome.

source.quote: Porcius Festus was the 5th procurator of Judea from about 59 to 62

events.title: Nero becomes emperor
events.summary: The last emperor of Augustus's line rules Rome. Christian tradition says Peter and Paul died under him.

source.quote: was Roman emperor from AD 54 until his suicide in AD 68

events.title: The Great Fire of Rome
events.summary: Fire destroys much of the city. Nero blames the Christians and has many put to death.

source.quote: began on the evening of 18-19 July 64 AD

events.title: The Jewish revolt against Rome begins
events.summary: Riots in Caesarea grow into a full revolt. Rome answers with an army that will destroy Jerusalem.

source.quote: The First Jewish-Roman War (66-73/74 CE)

events.title: Rome takes Masada
events.summary: Romans build a great ramp to the desert fortress. Josephus says the defenders died rather than surrender.

source.quote: allowing the Romans to breach the wall of the fortress on April 16, 73 AD

events.title: The Arch of Titus shows the temple's spoils
events.summary: A triumphal arch in Rome shows soldiers carrying the temple's menorah from Jerusalem.

source.quote: 81 AD by Emperor Domitian shortly after the death of his older brother Titus

events.title: Domitian rules Rome
events.summary: Many scholars date John's exile on Patmos and the book of Revelation to his reign.

source.quote: was Roman emperor from 81 to 96

events.title: Josephus completes the Antiquities of the Jews
events.summary: A Jewish historian in Rome retells Israel's story for Greek readers. He mentions John the Baptist and James.

source.quote: completed during the 13th year of the reign of the Emperor Flavius Domitian, around AD 93 to 94

events.title: The Bar Kokhba revolt
events.summary: A last Jewish revolt is crushed by Hadrian. Jews are barred from Jerusalem, renamed Aelia Capitolina.

source.quote: The Bar Kokhba Revolt (132-136 CE)

events.title: Izapa at its height
events.summary: A ceremonial center near the Pacific coast of Chiapas carves narrative stelae. Its style links the Olmec and the Maya.

source.quote: The site reached its apogee between 850 BCE and 100 BCE

events.title: Kaminaljuyu flourishes in highland Guatemala
events.summary: A great highland city builds canals and mounds in the Valley of Guatemala. It trades widely across the region.

events.title: Early Maya kingship at Takalik Abaj
events.summary: A trading city on Guatemala's Pacific slope raises carved monuments. Olmec and Maya styles meet there.

source.quote: Takalik Abaj is representative of the first blossoming of Maya culture that had occurred by about 400 BC.

events.title: The San Bartolo murals
events.summary: Painters cover a temple room with a Maya creation story and an early king. Some of the oldest Maya writing is found here.

source.quote: they date to the 3rd century BC

events.title: The Nazca Lines are drawn
events.summary: People on Peru's desert coast scrape huge lines and figures into the ground. Many can be seen whole only from the air.

source.quote: They were created between 500 BC and 500 AD

events.title: The oldest known Long Count date
events.summary: A carved panel in Chiapas records a date in the Mesoamerican Long Count calendar. No earlier example is known.

source.quote: The oldest Mesoamerican Long Count calendar date yet discovered, December 36 BCE, was found on Stela 2

events.title: Stela C of Tres Zapotes
events.summary: A Gulf Coast monument bears a Long Count date and Epi-Olmec writing. It shows Olmec traditions living on.

source.quote: correlates in the Gregorian calendar to September 3, 32 BCE

events.title: The Hopewell mound builders
events.summary: Peoples of the Ohio valley build great earthworks. They trade copper, shell, and mica across the continent.

source.quote: The Portsmouth Earthworks were constructed from 100 BCE to 500 CE.

events.title: La Mojarra Stela 1
events.summary: A Veracruz monument carries a long text in Epi-Olmec script. It shows a ruler in elaborate dress.

source.quote: a Mesoamerican carved monument (stela) dating from 156 CE

events.title: The Pyramid of the Sun rises at Teotihuacan
events.summary: Builders raise one of the largest pyramids in the Americas. Teotihuacan becomes the great power of central Mexico.

source.quote: It is believed to have been constructed about 200 AD.

events.title: The Xitle volcano buries Cuicuilco
events.summary: Lava covers a city in the Valley of Mexico. Its people scatter, and Teotihuacan grows stronger.

source.quote: The site was occupied until its destruction by the eruption of Xitle, sometime between 245 and 315 CE.

events.title: Teotihuacan's general reaches Tikal
events.summary: Siyaj K'ak' arrives at Tikal, and its king dies the same day. New rulers tied to Teotihuacan take power.

source.quote: In 378 and 379, he oversaw the replacing of the kings of important Maya states
